title: R Interface to FishBase
text: Welcome rfishbase 5! fourth rewrite original rfishbase package described Boettiger et al. (2012). Another streamlined re-design following new abilities data hosting access. release uses Source Cooperative S3 storage data metadata hosting parquet format, providing improved reliability resolving firewall issues users experienced previous hosting solutions. Data access simplified direct S3 API queries instead previous contentid-based resolution. allows metadata defined alongside data, platform independent R package. simplified access protocol relies duckdbfs direct reads tables. Several functions previously used manage connections now deprecated removed, along significant number dependencies. Core use still centers around package API using fb_tbl() function, legacy helper functions common tables like species() still accessible can still optionally filter species name appropriate. , loading full tables sub-setting manually still recommended. Historic helper functions like load_taxa() (combining taxonomic classification Species, Genus, Family Order tables), validate_names(), common_to_sci() sci_to_common() working order, using table-based outputs. rfishbase 1.0 relied parsing XML pages served directly Fishbase.org. rfishbase 2.0 relied calls ruby-based API, fishbaseapi, provided access SQL snapshots 20 popular tables FishBase SeaLifeBase. rfishbase 3.0 side-stepped API making queries directly downloaded compressed csv tables static web host. substantially improved performance reliability, particularly large queries. release largely remained backwards compatible 2.0, added tables. rfishbase 4.0 extends static model interface. Static tables distributed parquet accessed provenance-based identifier. old functions retained, new interface introduced provide easy access fishbase tables. welcome feedback, issues questions users may encounter issues tracker GitHub: https://github.com/ropensci/rfishbase/issues

title: length_length — length_length
text: table contains relationships conversion one length type another 8,000 species fish, derived different publications, e.g. Moutopoulos Stergiou (2002) Gaygusuz et al (2006), fish pictures, e.g. Collette Nauen (1983), Compagno (1984) Randall (1997). relationships, always refer centimeters, may consist either regression linking two length types, form: Length type (2) = + b x Length type (1) Length type (2) = b' x Length type (1) available length types , elsewhere FishBase, TL = total length; FL = fork length; SL = standard length; WD = width (rays); OT = type (specified Comment field). version equation (1) presented, length range, number fish used regression, sex correlation coefficient presented, available. version equation (2) presented, range correlation coefficient omitted, ratio (2) usually estimated single specimen, fish covering narrow range lengths. Note column naming: columns Length1 Length2 follow FishBase's internal database convention, may appear counterintuitive. Length1 unknown length predicted, Length2 known length used predictor. formula therefore: Length1 = + b * Length2. matches FishBase website, labels columns "Unknown length" "Known length" respectively.
